GEOL 3032.title: Introduction to Sedimentology and Depositional Environments

prereq_rule.text: GEOL 1202, or GEOL 1003 and GEOL 1602; credit or registration in GEOL 2081 or GEOL 3200; or permission of department.

THTR 7622.title: Scenery Automation
THTR 7622.description: Examination of scenery control systems, including PLC programming, positioning control, software and all in-one control systems.

OCS 7125.title: Estuarine Dynamics

PSYC 7925.title: Psychological Assessment II
PSYC 7925.prereq: PSYC 7125 or equivalent; graduate standing in clinical psychology or consent of instructor.
PSYC 7925.description: Administration and interpretation of objective and projective tests of personality and psychopathology; neuropsychological assessment techniques.

MEDP 7270.title: Advanced Radiation Therapy Physics

SOCL 4551.title: Global Society

HIST 2025.title: Early Modern Europe 3

OCS 7129.description: Impact of projected global climate change on stability and functioning of coastal and interior wetland ecosystems; feedback of biogeochemical changes in wetlands caused by climate change.

BIOL 7648.title: Museum Field Expedition

THTR 7802.title: Properties II

ENGL 7922.title: Authors Seminar

PHIL 4914.title: Philosophy of Language

PHIL 4914.description: Various theories of meaning, their implications and presuppositions and their relevance to issues in such areas as theory of perception, theory of truth, metaphysics, ethics, philosophy of mind and action.

prereq_rule.text: one logic course or consent of instructor.

DART 7004.title: Introduction to Material Culture Studies
DART 7004.description: Research and discussion seminar on the study of materiality as an integral dimension of culture through focus on the social and cultural roles of physical things, the built environment and cultural landscape.

HIST 4028.title: The First World War

FIN 7550.title: Theory of Finance

ANSC 3060.title: Companion Animal Health Maintenance and Disease

ANSC 3060.description: Canine and feline health maintenance programs, diagnostic tests and tools used in animal health professions, etiology, clinical findings, diagnosis, prevention and treatment of common companion animal diseases and disorders, zoonotic disease transmission and prevention.

SPAN 3074.title: Advanced Readings on Hispanic-American Civilization

INTL 3001.title: Gateway to International Studies
other: Required for all international studies majors.

LIS 7002.title: Information Resources

ENGL 4080.title: Studies in Modernism

CMST 4160.title: Persuasive Communication

TAM 3042.title: Retail Buying and Merchandise Management

PHIL 7903.title: Seminar in Continental Philosophy

RNR 2063.title: Introductory Internship in Natural Resources

UNIV 0000.title: University courses
UNIV 0000.description: Unique courses of timely and general interest are offered periodically as “University” courses. These courses are interdisciplinary, broad in scope and centered on topics of current concern. Permission to offer a UNIV course must be obtained from the Office of Academic Affairs and the course must be approved by the Faculty Senate Courses and Curricula Committee. University courses may not be offered more than twice (with the exception of The Boyd Professor Lecture Series). Each course carries undergraduate credit of one to three semester hours. Acceptance of such credit toward fulfillment of degree requirements is decided by the faculty of each college or school within the university. The topic, credit and class time of each university course are announced by the Office of Academic Affairs prior to the beginning of the semester in which the course is to be taught. University courses have been offered on such topics as The Constitution: Then and Now (1987), The Age of the French Revolution (1989), Diversity in America (1990), The Holocaust (1992), Political Communication (1993), Race Relations (1995) and The Boyd Professor Lecture Series (2000).

repeatable: May be taken for a max. of 6 sem. hrs. when topics vary.
EDCI 4466.description: Critical issues in the nature of knowledge and inquiry in school subjects: English, mathematics, science and social studies.

KIN 1600.title: Individual Wellness and Public Health
other: This is an Integrative Learning Core (ILC) course that awards general education credit.
KIN 1600.description: Content and theory related to basic health information; critical health issues; economic, political and cultural influences on health and wellness; improving and maintaining optimal health and wellness.

AGRO 4056.title: Microbial Ecology and Nutrient Cycling in Soils
equivalent_courses: Also offered as BIOL 4256 and EMS 4056.
AGRO 4056.description: Microorganisms in terrestrial environments and biogenic processes influencing C, N, S and P cycling; role of microorganisms in biological nitrogen fixation, plant nutrient availability, formation of soil humus and decomposition of organic and inorganic materials; impact of microbial processes on environmental quality.

HIST 4032.title: The Balkans: 1879-Present
HIST 4032.description: Events leading up to and including World War I, problems of the inter-war period, World War II and rise and decline of Communism in Southeastern Europe.

ID 3652.title: HONORS: Interior Design Studio III
equivalent_courses: Same as ID 3752, with special emphasis for qualified Honors students. Credit will not be given for this course and ID 3752.
other: Required field trip. Students are responsible for paying travel expenses associated with the course.

FREN 1201.title: Elementary Louisiana French I
restricted_credits: Credit will not be given for both FREN 1001 and FREN 1201 nor for both FREN 1002 and FREN 1202. Students with previous study of French should take the French placement exam. Student who do not place in FREN 1002 or higher through the placement exam should enroll in FREN 1201.
other: This is an Integrative Learning Core (ILC) course that awards general education credit.
FREN 1201.description: Basic lexicon and structure of Louisiana French; emphasis on communicative language use; supplementary work in language laboratory.

MC 4550.title: Social Media Analysis & Creation
MC 4550.prereq: MC 2035, majors and minors only or permission of department.
MC 4550.description: How to use social media analytics to create effective and interactive content.

BE 4989.title: Independent Study in Biological Engineering
BE 4989.prereq: senior standing. Written engineering report required.
repeatable: May be taken for a max. of 6 sem. hrs. of credit when topics vary.
BE 4989.description: Biological engineering practice; library research, experimental and/or theoretical investigation.

prereq_rule.text: senior standing. Written engineering report required.

VMED 5132.title: Microscopic Anatomy
VMED 5132.description: The histology of the basic tissues of the body and the microscopic anatomy of the organ systems in domestic mammals with consideration of the organ-specific microscopic structures covering the respiratory and urogenital organs, digestive system, defense and sensory organs, and skin.

SW 7503.title: Specialized Field Internship II
SW 7503.prereq: completion of all Generalist courses; majors only and credit for or concurrent registration in SW 7502  & SW 7505.
SW 7503.description: Supervised internship in an approved agency setting where advanced knowledge, skills, values and ethics are applied in the practice setting. 240 clock hours.

prereq_rule.text: completion of all Generalist courses; majors only and credit for or concurrent registration in SW 7502  & SW 7505.

EDCI 3640.title: Dual Certification General/Special Education Student Teaching: Grades 1-5
EDCI 3640.prereq: See " Requirements for Student Teaching." Passage of Praxis 5002, 5003, 5004, 5005, 5543 and 5622.
other: 1 hr. lecture; 30 hrs. internship in diverse classroom settings.
EDCI 3640.description: All day, all semester, all subject student teaching experience in general and special education, including observation, participation, and direct teaching under supervision of an assigned public school mentor teacher team and LSU faculty/staff member.

prereq_rule.text: See " Requirements for Student Teaching." Passage of Praxis 5002, 5003, 5004, 5005, 5543 and 5622.

ENGL 2201.title: Introduction to World Literary Traditions
other: [LCCN: CENL 2203, 2223, World Literature I, Major World Writers]
This is an Integrative Learning Core (ILC) course that awards general education credit.

AEEE 7701.title: Grantseeking in Agricultural & Extension Education
AEEE 7701.description: The purpose of the course is to engage in the proposal development process required to seek funding from foundation and government agencies. As such, students will conceptualize innovative projects that address societal needs, identify funding sources, and develop proposals that follow agency guidelines, including a literature review, need for the project, approach, timeline, and budget.

CSC 4700.title: Special Topics in Computer Science
repeatable: May be taken for a max. of 9 cr. hrs. when topics vary. Total hrs. earned in CSC 2700, CSC 3700, and 4700 should not exceed 9 hrs.
CSC 4700.description: Specialized areas of current interest in computer science.

ELRC 7603.title: Leadership in Higher Education
ELRC 7603.description: Analysis of leadership issues and theory relating to postsecondary education, including the college presidency and academic governance; institutional culture; student diversity, curricular change and new providers of higher education.

CSC 1250.title: Introduction to Programming
restricted_credits: Credit will not be given for this course and CSC 1253 or CSC 1350.
CSC 1250.description: Fundamentals of problem solving, program design, algorithms and programming using a high-level language.

ME 4223.title: Welding Engineering II

ME 4223.description: Fundamentals and intermediate level welding and joining; intermediate nondestructive evaluation emphasizing phased-array-ultrasonics; design calculations of welded structures; advanced welding processes.

prereq_rule.text: ME 2733; ME 3633; ME 4213 or consent of instructor; grade of "C" or better in ENGL 1001.

LA 7044.title: Ecology and Technology IV
LA 7044.description: Construction practices in landscape architecture, focusing on the primary components of built environments: materials, assemblies, and technique; the principles of sustainability as it relates to construction and materials; advanced materials and emerging technologies.

prereq_rule.text: LA 7034 or consent of School.

THTR 1701.title: Introduction to Entertainment Industries
THTR 1701.description: An introduction to the structure and internal organization of the entertainment industries. Attention is given to practical application based on theoretical and historical foundations. This course also serves as an introduction to the uses and influences of technology in entertainment with attention to innovations, history, and technology's effects on the global entertainment industries.

GEOL 4182.title: Physical Hydrogeology
GEOL 4182.prereq: MATH 1550 or MATH 1551 or MATH 1540 or MATH 1510.
GEOL 4182.description: Subsurface fluid flow in geological materials; emphasis on geological controls of the origin and migration of pore water, including saline brines, in sedimentary basins; topics including crustal scale flow, petroleum migration, ore formation and subsurface flow regimes in Louisiana

AGRI 1011.title: Issues in Agriculture
AGRI 1011.prereq: Enrollment in this course is limited to freshmen in the Agriculture Residential College or by permission of department.
AGRI 1011.description: Exploring prevalent issues in all fields of agriculture and agricultural research.

prereq_rule.text: Enrollment in this course is limited to freshmen in the Agriculture Residential College or by permission of department.

MUS 2020.title: Jazz and the American Experience
MUS 2020.description: Development of jazz music from the 20th century to current day and its relationship to the American Experience.

MUS 7921.title: Seminar in Music Theory

repeatable: May be taken for a max. of 6 sem. hrs. of credit applicable to the MM degree when topics vary and only 12 additional sem. hrs. of credit applicable to the PhD when topics vary.

PETE 7280.title: Mathematical Simulation of Petroleum Reservoir Performance

HIST 4161.title: Religion in the United States

RNR 7020.title: Ecology of Fishes
RNR 7020.description: Ecology of fish populations; interactions of fishes and their environment; behavioral adaptations of fishes.

ME 3633.title: Manufacturing Processes & Methods

prereq_rule.text: IE 1002 or "C" or better in ME 1222; ME 2733.

ARCH 5004.title: Concentration Seminar
repeatable: May be taken for a max. of 9 hrs. of credit when topics vary.

EDCI 7760.title: Nature and Needs of the Gifted and Talented
EDCI 7760.description: Historical perspective, social, emotional and educational characteristics; administrative considerations; sociological and psychological studies; special populations.

LATN 4002.title: Roman Satire
LATN 4002.description: Readings from Petronius' Satyricon, Martial and Juvenal for their humor, with attention to evidence of the lives and language of ordinary Roman people.

CE 7490.title: Damage Mechanics in Metals and Matrix Composites
CE 7490.description: Theoretical formulation and application of the different constitutive models to metals and metal matrix composites but with consideration of other materials; analysis of isotropic and anisotropic damage in materials.

AEEE 4011.title: Communications in Agricultural & Extension Education
AEEE 4011.description: Synthesis and application of concepts and principles of communication in the extension educational program.

ENGL 4475.title: American Folklore
ENGL 4475.description: Folklore of the U.S., including regional, racial, ethnic and occupational groups; relation of folklore to other aspects of American vernacular culture and to American literature.

KIN 1224.title: Tennis
KIN 1224.prereq: KIN majors only until priority scheduling ends.
other: All basic activity courses are offered on a pass/fail grade basis.

prereq_rule.text: KIN majors only until priority scheduling ends.

ART 4655.title: Advanced Jewelry/Metalsmithing

repeatable: May be taken for a max. of 15 hrs. of credit.
other: Registration for all multiple-credit courses taken for over three credits in a given semester will require the prior permission of the instructor.
Students are responsible for studio fee associated with course.
ART 4655.description: Advanced studio work in one specific process such as: forging, forming, reproduction processes, advanced construction techniques, CAD/CAM, mechanisms, clasps, chain construction. Emphasis on historical and contemporary aesthetic in art jewelry and metalsmithing.

prereq_rule.text: consent of instructor based on review of student's portfolio.

ECON 4220.title: Wage and Employment Analysis
ECON 4220.description: The labor market; labor supply and demand, human capital, racial and sex discrimination, effects of minimum wage laws, causes of various wage and employment differentials.

prereq_rule.text: ECON 2000 and ECON 2010; or ECON 2030.

THTR 7923.title: Seminar in Gender, Sexuality and Performance
THTR 7923.description: Survey of practical and theoretical approaches, attitudes, and debates regarding issues of gender and sexuality as they relate to performance.

HORT 4040.title: International Horticulture
other: This course is part of ACCEPtS.
HORT 4040.description: This course will provide an overview of the horticulture industry worldwide. Export, marketing and international trade issues will be covered in a global horticultural context.

CE 7740.title: Master's Report
CE 7740.description: Comprehensive report with oral defense on subject approved by the major professor.

MUS 7725.title: Survey of Symphonic Literature I
MUS 7725.description: A survey of orchestral works beginning with the Baroque period of music and ending with the early Romantic; emphasis on preparation for performance.

COMD 7281.title: Acquired Neurogenic Language Disorders
COMD 7281.description: Neuroscience, assessment, and treatment of acquired neurogenic language disorders (aphasia and dementia).

CM 4440.title: Advanced Construction Technologies
CM 4440.description: An overview of some of the commercial and emerging construction technologies which are used for infrastructure development. Hardware, software, and material related innovations for cutting-edge construction technologies such as Construction 3D Printing are presented. The advantages which are offered by these technologies to realize a more efficient construction process, as well as existing challenges are discussed in detail.

REL 4035.title: Women & Buddhism
REL 4035.description: Buddhist concepts of women in comparative socio-historical contexts. Critical analyses of practices, teachings, and interpretive frames.

HNRS 2406.title: Renaissance to Enlightenment
other: This is an Integrative Learning Core (ILC) course that awards general education credit.
HNRS 2406.description: Western civilization from the Renaissance through the Enlightenment. Includes literature, history, philosophy, religion, government, and fine arts.

MUS 7703.title: Contemporary Musical Practices
other: 6 sem. hrs. applicable to the MM degree when topics vary; 6 additional sem. hrs. applicable to the DMA degree when topics vary.
MUS 7703.description: Compositional trends in contemporary music; discussion of books on composition; analysis of major compositions.

PLHL 7010.title: Plant Molecular Biology

PLHL 7010.description: Molecular biology, biochemistry and genetics of higher plants and plant-associated microorganisms; genome organization and structure in nuclei, chloroplasts and mitochondria; structure and expression of plant genes under control of developmental and environmental signals; plant interactions with pathogenic and symbiotic microorganisms.

prereq_rule.text: BIOL 3060, BIOL 4093 and BIOL 4094; or equivalent.

ENGL 3080.title: Post-colonial Literature
ENGL 3080.description: Survey of literature from former British colonies in South Asia, Africa and the Caribbean; colonialism; nationalism; independence; diaspora; transnationalism; hybridity; women’s rights; building a new nation, etc.

CMST 7946.title: Theory and Performance of Narrative Discourse
CMST 7946.description: Narrative theory in literature and performance; rhetoric of narrative discourse.

KIN 2400.title: Introduction to Sports Medicine
KIN 2400.description: Students interested in pursuing careers in sports medicine will learn about basic aspects of health care, including the roles and responsibilities of the sports medicne team, best practicies in sports safety, and basic injury management.

ELRC 7614.title: College Access and Choice
ELRC 7614.description: Provides broad overview of access to postsecondary education and factors related to students' college choice decisions. Covers policies, programs, and other initiatives aimed at addressing the college access problem in the United States.

AGRO 7067.title: Crop Breeding Practicum
repeatable: May be taken for a max. of 4 hrs. of credit when topics vary; consent of instructor.
AGRO 7067.description: Application of plant breeding techniques for agronomic and horticultural crops, emphasis on visits to practicing public and commercial programs.

EE 7798.title: Distributed Computing

HIST 2014.title: Goddesses to Witches: Women in Europe 500 BCE -1700 CE

AGEC 4443.title: Farm and Rural Land Appraisal

ELRC 7348.title: Counseling Skills for Substance Use Problems

PHYS 4132.title: Electromagnetism and Electromagnetic Waves
PHYS 4132.description: Emphasis on electromagnetic waves and radiation.

Section 2 introduced students to different parts of the cardiovascular system including blood and its constituents. Section 3 deals with respiratory gas exchange and how this is regulated during homeostasis and how it is altered in disease.

FREN 4403.title: Instructional Strategies for the Second Language French Classroom

MUS 9001.title: Doctoral Solo Recital

TAM 7030.title: Creativity in Product Development
TAM 7030.description: Examination, enhancement and application of creativity in the product development process with interdisciplinary application. Exploration of creative innovators and their design processes resulting in design, development and execution of original product.

ACCT 7270.title: Statement and Report Presentation and Analysis
other: MS in accounting students or permission of department.

LHRD 7602.description: Systematic application of social research procedures for evaluating the conceptualization, design, implementation and utility of human resource and organization development programs.

restricted_credits: Credit will not be given for this course and CE 2451.

LATN 2066.title: Golden Age Prose

EDCI 7143.title: The Teaching of Literature in Secondary Schools

ARCH 4031.title: Architectural Structures III

GEOG 4037.description: Geographic survey of natural environment, population and economy of China and its relationships to the rest of the world.

PHIL 4942.title: Topics in Meta-Ethics

repeatable: May be taken for a max. of 6 sem. hrs. of credit when topics vary.

MUTH 3400.description: Professional and administrative skills and their applications in the Music Therapy profession. Skills for creating a website, resume, budget, and interviewing.

GEOG 2050.title: Physical Geography: The Atmosphere
repeatable: May be taken for elective geology credit.
other: This is an Integrative Learning Core (ILC) course that awards general education credit.

EDCI 1750.title: Integrative Community Studies Program and Campus Orientation

other: This course is open for enrollment of Integrative Community Studies students only.

HORT 2061.title: Plant Propagation
other: This is an Integrative Learning Core (ILC) course that awards general education credit.

prereq_rule.text: HORT 2050 or concurrent enrollment.

prereq_rule.text: calculus and linear algebra or concurrent enrollment in ECON 7610.

ART 4661.title: Advanced Ceramics

repeatable: May be taken for a max. of 9 sem. hrs. of credit.
other: Students are responsible for studio fee associated with course.

prereq_rule.text: valid Advanced Lifesaving Certificate.

LIS 7618.title: E-Discovery

CFS 3070.title: Intimate Relationships
CFS 3070.description: Introduction to the individual and contextual factors affecting the formation and maintenance of intimate relationships.

ENGL 4062.title: Studies in the Victorian Age

FREN 4060.title: French Literature of Quebec
FREN 4060.prereq: FREN 3071 and FREN 3072 or equivalents; or permission of instructor.
FREN 4060.description: Major aspects of the literature of Quebec.

prereq_rule.text: FREN 3071 and FREN 3072 or equivalents; or permission of instructor.

GEOG 4080.title: Historical Geography
GEOG 4080.description: Advanced concepts and principles of historical geography.

ANTH 2050.title: World Archaeology

ANTH 2050.description: Survey of human culture history from the stone age to the present; spread of humanity around the globe; major cultural developments including hunting and gathering, origins of agriculture, discovery and spread of metalworking, rise of ancient civilizations, and development of the modern world.

RNR 2900.title: Horticultural Botany

ACCT 4236.title: Environmental, Social, and Governance
ACCT 4236.description: The study of Environmental, Social, and Governance based on the United Nation's 10 Principles and 17 Goals of Sustainability of ESG and SEC disclosure requirements.

PBS 7530.title: Laboratory Animal Science I

GEOG 4014.description: Climatic phenomena; methods in development of regional climatology.

ME 7533.title: Numerical Methods in Applied Mechanics
ME 7533.description: Computer methods used to solve engineering problems; advanced numerical methods.

GRAD 7004.title: Learning Through Effective Teaching

EDCI 7761.title: Models and Strategies for Teaching the Gifted
EDCI 7761.description: Examination of models, teaching strategies and resources for planning appropriate learning experiences for gifted and talented students in diverse settings.

LA 2401.title: Landscape Ecology

CHE 4162.title: Unit Operations Laboratory

AAAS 2050.title: Contemporary Africa

ART 7020.title: Special Topics Graduate Studio
repeatable: May be taken for a max. of 12 sem. hrs. of credit.

GEOL 4051.title: Computer Programming and Data Analysis in Earth Sciences
GEOL 4051.description: Computer programming and application of data analysis principles to problems in Earth Sciences.

POLI 4080.title: American Political Thought

ANSC 2093.title: Dairy Products Judging

FREN 7170.title: Studies in Belgian Francophone Literature and Culture
repeatable: May be taken for a maximum of 6 hrs. credit with approval of the department, if content of the course varies.

CMST 7914.title: Communication in Health Care Contexts
repeatable: May be taken for a max. of 6 sem. hrs. of credit when topics vary.

MUS 4766.title: Marching Band Techniques
MUS 4766.description: Charting techniques for marching band; emphasis on contemporary drill design, practical projects in charting drill.

ITAL 3071.title: Survey of Italian Literature

ENGL 2029.title: Drama

BIOL 7901.title: Departmental Seminar in Biological Sciences
repeatable: May be repeated for a max. of 6 sem. hrs. of credit.

SPAN 2155.title: Spanish Language and Culture

SPAN 2155.description: Oral and written commentary on a variety of genres and nonprint media in Spanish. Designed for students who learned Spanish as a second language in a school setting.

MATH 7350.title: Complex Analysis
MATH 7350.description: Theory of holomorphic functions of one complex variable; path integrals, power series, singularities, mapping properties, normal families, other topics.

KIN 7545.title: Economic Issues in Sports
KIN 7545.description: In-depth examination focusing on the economic issues of professional, intercollegiate, and recreational sport around the world; examining specific areas such as competitive balance of sports leagues, discrimination, and the demand for sport.

CMST 2060.title: Public Speaking
other: This is an Integrative Learning Core (ILC) course that awards general education credit.
CMST 2060.description: Develop skills needed by the effective communicator and critical consumer of speech. Includes practice in speaking and an introduction to theories and analysis of speeches.

ARTH 4410.title: Later Greek Art
ARTH 4410.description: Greek art from the time of Themistocles to the age of Augustus.

ID 4765.title: Interior Design Professional Residency

CLST 3090.title: Comparative Mythology
CLST 3090.description: Introduction to myths from around the world with comparisons to Greek and Roman mythology.

THTR 7227.title: MFA Voice Studio I
THTR 7227.description: Vocal foundations. The vocal training progression begins by exploring fundamental voice skills for the actor through the mind-body-voice connection, vocal health, respiration, phonation, resonation, articulation, and contemporary text.

prereq_rule.text: admission to the MFA program.

MATH 1100.title: The Nature of Mathematics
other: This is an Integrative Learning Core (ILC) course that awards general education credit.

MATH 1100.description: Using mathematics to solve problems and reason quantitatively. Topics include set theory, logic, personal finance, and elementary number theory.

ACCT 3021.title: Intermediate Accounting–Part II
ACCT 3021.prereq: grade of “C” or above in ACCT 3001 or ACCT 3002.
other: Continuation of ACCT 3001 / ACCT 3002. Credit will not be given if credit was earned from ACCT 7011.
ACCT 3021.description: Accounting for liabilities, income taxes, pensions, leases, stockholders' equity, earnings per share, accounting changes and corrections of errors, and income and balance sheet presentations.

prereq_rule.text: grade of “C” or above in ACCT 3001 or ACCT 3002.

PHYS 2109.title: General Physics Laboratory

restricted_credits: Credit will not be given for both this course and PHYS 1209. Laboratory to accompany PHYS 2002 and

MUS 3018.title: Vocal Pedagogy

prereq_rule.text: 12 sem. hrs. of applied voice study.

NFS 4040.title: Quality Assurance in the Food Industry

CE 4420.title: Principles of Prestressed Concrete
CE 4420.description: Analysis and design of prestressed concrete structural elements; full and partial prestressing; service ability and strength requirements; code criteria for bridges, buildings and other structures.

ENTM 4100.title: Insect Behavior
ENTM 4100.description: Current and classical concepts in behavioral theory; communication systems; stimuli orientation, social interaction; aspects of insect control using behavior modification.

LA 7051.title: Advanced Topics I

prereq_rule.text: a grade of "C" or better in CHE 3102 or equivalent introductory course in transport science.

EE 7510.title: Advanced Linear Systems
EE 7510.description: Modern approaches for the analysis and identification of linear, discrete and continuous time, control systems; state variable and fractional description techniques, functional analytic methods.

AEEE 4102.title: Teaching Methods in Agricultural & Extension Education
AEEE 4102.description: Recognized methods of instruction and presentation in agricultural education, including the selection of teaching aids and support materials, strategies for working with diverse learners, and classroom management.

PHIL 2033.title: History of Ancient and Medieval Philosophy
equivalent_courses: An honors course, PHIL 2053, is also available.
restricted_credits: Credit will not be given for this course and PHIL 2053.

PETE 7212.title: Well Completion Design
PETE 7212.description: Systems analysis for optimum production by designing best combination of tubing, flow lines, choke sizes, perforation density and separator pressure; inflow performance of reservoirs; well completion techniques; gravel packing; tubing effects.

MGT 4440.title: International Strategic Management
other: Reserved for College of Business students; open to others with permission of department.
MGT 4440.description: This course examines how businesses approach managing organizations in the global context. OCS 4308.title: Plants in Coastal Environments

OCS 4308.description: Ecology of Louisiana's major coastal plant communities; emphasis on influence of environmental factors controlling plant distribution and productivity; physiological, morphological and anatomical mechanisms aiding plant survival; man's impact on Louisiana's coastal plant communities.

prereq_rule.text: one-semester course in biology or ecology or consent of instructor.

RNR 7012.title: Ecology and Management of Waterfowl
restricted_credits: Credit will not be given for this course and RNR 4012.

EXST 7047.title: Structural Equation Modeling and Hierarchical Linear Modeling

AEEE 3722.title: Group Process and Facilitation Skills
AEEE 3722.description: Understanding youth and adult group dynamics; models of decision making and group consensus skills. Focus on acquiring and refining facilitation skills needed to lead groups through goal setting and goal attainment.

PETE 3085.title: Well Performance and Production

NFS 7050.title: Food Protein Biotechnology

AEEE 1002.title: Developing Professional Confidence: Passion, Purpose and Planning

THTR 4540.title: Advanced Sound Design

DMAE 7270.title: Capstone Production Team

ME 2733.title: Materials of Engineering

Form and Function 2 will cover a) the cavities and spaces of the body and the organ systems within and b) the head and organ systems within.

ENGL 4001.title: Intermediate Creative Nonfiction Workshop

ISDS 7070.title: Seminar in Advanced Business Problems

ATRN 7204.title: Primary Care Medicine
other: Master of Science in Athletic Training majors only.
